content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Parsing transforms text into values; serialization turns values back into text. File tools, query languages, streaming patterns, and structural comparison each solve different problems, so choose tooling based on input size and intended operation.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly addresses: What serialization means. Turning in-memory data into JSON text. Serialization of strings, numbers, and booleans.; Object and array serialization. Unicode output. Pretty-printing. Handling values unsupported by JSON.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: JSON Serialization
content_blocks.code:
import json

value = {"name": "Mira", "active": True}
text = json.dumps(value, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
print(text)
content_blocks.expected_output: The example serializes an in-memory Python mapping to formatted JSON text and preserves Unicode characters with ensure_ascii=False.
